questions.question: Which BBS software is this board built on?
questions.note: Written by Joe Hodge for the Amiga, and running here in a browser.

questions.question: Teletext was broadcast in which part of the TV signal?
questions.note: The black bar between frames. About 30 bytes per line, 25 frames a second.

questions.question: How many columns wide is a teletext page?
questions.note: 40 columns by 24 rows, seven bits per character.

questions.question: What was the BBC's teletext service called?
questions.note: Ceefax ran from 1974 to 2012. Oracle was ITV and Channel 4.

questions.question: Which game did Team17 build for teletext in 1996?
questions.note: Every possible screen was drawn in advance and broadcast as hidden pages. It was shelved because a day's broadcast could not hold enough of them.

questions.question: What is a teletext block graphic made of?
questions.note: Which makes a whole page 80 by 72 pixels.

questions.question: Which quiz was Teletext's best known game?
questions.note: Bamboozle was a page graph: each answer was simply a page number to jump to.

questions.question: How does a teletext page hide an answer until you ask?
questions.note: Conceal is a spacing attribute. The text is really on the page - the decoder just refuses to draw it.

questions.question: What are the four fastext keys?
questions.note: Carried in packet 27. An unused link is written as page 8FF.

questions.question: Most surviving teletext pages were recovered from what?
questions.note: Enthusiasts pull the data back out of the blanking interval on old recordings, errors and all.

questions.question: Which Channel 4 teletext page was famous for games writing?
questions.note: Digitiser ran on Channel 4 teletext from 1993, and was funnier than it had any need to be.

questions.question: A teletext page number is written in which base?
questions.note: Magazine 1-8 and two hex digits, so pages like 1A0 are real - a remote just had no way to type them.
